summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with primary progressive multiple sclerosis and neurogenic bladder managed with a suprapubic catheter, was admitted with a complicated urinary tract infection following a recent course of antibiotics for a resistant E. coli infection. He presented with fever, tachycardia, and hand tremors, without urinary symptoms. Laboratory findings showed leukocytosis and a contaminated urine culture. He was treated initially with IV piperacillin-tazobactam and transitioned to oral Bactrim based on prior sensitivities. His infection resolved, with normalization of vital signs and white blood cell count. The speech and swallow team evaluated his stable dysphagia and recommended a ground diet with thin liquids. He was discharged home on a 7-day course of Bactrim and advised to follow up with infectious disease to discuss long-term prophylaxis.
